title: Filtered torsion union
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $F$ be a torsion sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on $X_{\Et}$, i.e. an object of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ every local section of which is locally killed by a positive integer. Then

$$
 F=\varinjlim_{(\mathbf N_{>0},\mid)}F[n],\qquad
 F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)\ \text{[def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]},
$$

as a filtered colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$: the canonical map $c_F:\varinjlim_nF[n]\to F$ induced by the inclusions $F[n]\hookrightarrow F$ is an isomorphism. Here positive integers are ordered
by divisibility, and for $n\mid m$ the transition map is the inclusion
$F[n]\hookrightarrow F[m]$; this poset is filtered because
$\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)$ is a common upper bound.

proof.text: *The diagram and the canonical map.* By [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel] $F[n]$ is the subsheaf $U\mapsto\{s\in F(U):ns=0\}$ of $F$, with inclusion $i_n:F[n]\to F$. If $n\mid m$, write $m=kn$; then $ns=0$ implies $ms=k(ns)=0$, so $F[n]\subseteq F[m]$ as subsheaves of $F$, and the inclusion $j_{nm}:F[n]\to F[m]$ satisfies $i_m j_{nm}=i_n$; the inclusions compose, so $n\mapsto F[n]$ is a functor $D$ from the poset $(\mathbf N_{>0},\mid)$ to $\Ab(X_{\Et})$. This poset is nonempty and any $n,m$ have the upper bound $nm$; a poset has at most one arrow between two objects, so it is a filtered small category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ has all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], so $\varinjlim_nF[n]$ exists with coprojections $\iota_n$, and the compatible family $(i_n)$ induces the unique $c_F:\varinjlim_nF[n]\to F$ with $c_F\iota_n=i_n$ for all $n$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

*$c_F$ is a monomorphism.* The family $(i_n)$ is a natural transformation $i:D\to\Delta F$ to the constant diagram with value $F$, and each $i_n$ is a monomorphism (an inclusion of a subsheaf, injective on all sections). Filtered colimits in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ are exact, in particular a filtered colimit of monomorphisms is a monomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck] (the category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] is the category of abelian sheaves on the small etale site of that node). So $\varinjlim i:\varinjlim_nF[n]\to\varinjlim_n\Delta F$ is a monomorphism. The index category is filtered, hence connected (any two objects are joined by $n\to\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)\leftarrow m$), so the cocone $(\mathrm{id}_F)_n$ exhibits $F$ as the colimit of $\Delta F$ (a cocone $(\mu_n:F\to M)$ on $\Delta F$ has all $\mu_n$ equal along zigzags, and $\mu_n$ is then the unique factorization). Under this identification $\varinjlim i$ is the map with $(\varinjlim i)\iota_n=i_n$, i.e. $c_F$. Hence $c_F$ is a monomorphism. (The blueprint's sentence 'a section that is zero in $F$ is already zero in every $F[n]$' only shows that each $i_n$ is a monomorphism; the exactness of filtered colimits is what passes this to $c_F$.)

*$c_F$ is an epimorphism.* Let $U$ be an object of $X_{\Et}$ and $s\in F(U)$. Since $F$ is torsion [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], there are an etale covering $\{U_a\to U\}_a$ and integers $n_a\ge1$ with $n_a\,s|_{U_a}=0$. Then $s|_{U_a}\in F[n_a](U_a)$ by the sectionwise description of the kernel [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel]; call this section $t_a$, so $(i_{n_a})_{U_a}(t_a)=s|_{U_a}$. The section $g_a=(\iota_{n_a})_{U_a}(t_a)$ of $\varinjlim_nF[n]$ over $U_a$ satisfies $(c_F)_{U_a}(g_a)=(c_F\iota_{n_a})_{U_a}(t_a)=(i_{n_a})_{U_a}(t_a)=s|_{U_a}$ (step 1). Thus $c_F$ is locally surjective, and a locally surjective morphism of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ is an epimorphism [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective].

*Conclusion.* $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ is an abelian category [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and in an abelian category a morphism that is both a monomorphism and an epimorphism is an isomorphism (it is the kernel of its cokernel $0$, hence isomorphic to the identity). By steps 2 and 3, $c_F$ is an isomorphism, i.e. $F=\varinjlim_nF[n]$ via the inclusions.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every torsion sheaf $F$ the inclusions $F[n]\hookrightarrow F[mn]$ form a
filtered system and the canonical map $\varinjlim_nF[n]\to F$ is an
isomorphism.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
The transition map sends a section killed by $n$ to the same section, now
regarded as killed by $mn$. The map to $F$ is monic because a section that is
zero in $F$ is already zero in every $F[n]$. It is epic because every local
section of $F$ is locally killed by some positive integer and hence is locally in one
of the $F[n]$; sheafification preserves this local epimorphism.
